svg.text: full-size Perma-Proto (60 columns, rows a–j, breadboard topology) · ESP32-S3 socketed · 74AHCT125 · 8× piezo JST-XH · 3-pin LED strip JST · fed from the slab 5V rail

g.text: ● = solder joint · a line crossing without a dot is NOT connected

svg.text: 5V/GND pigtail (18–20 AWG) → WAGO 221 node on the slab DC rail
strain-relieve at the enclosure gland · the two vertical jumpers at left bridge top ↔ bottom rails
on two 1×22 female headers — pins in rows b & i, cols 3–24
◀ both USB ports face this edge (enclosure service side)
pin map = v1.1 silkscreen (USB left) — see protoboard_wiring.svg
col 3 (row a): GND → GND rail · col 4: 5V → +5V rail
8× ADC jumpers: GPIO col (free hole, row a/j) → S col, row i — map below, exact runs in protoboard_wiring.svg
pin 1 (1OE) → GND — or no data output!
◀ 3-wire harness to strip DIN (start of chain) — JST-XH 3-pin, pins in row a, cols 34/35/36

Board: full-size Perma-Proto (Adafruit 1606 — 157×51 mm, 60 columns) or a similar solderable breadboard-pattern PCB — the BOM's 5×7 cm half-size board is too small once the DevKitC-1 socket + 9 JST headers land.
Same topology as the Phase 2 breadboard: transfer the working bench circuit column-for-column; the power rails are pre-traced. JST-XH is 2.5 mm pitch on the 2.54 mm grid — no issue at 2–3 pins.

Enclosure: the board is 157 mm long — the BOM's ~110×60×30 mm box can't hold it. Use a ~190×110×60 mm box (e.g. Hammond 1591E); mount on standoffs via the board's mounting holes, USB end toward the service opening.

Piezo network per side: JST-XH 2-pin in row j (S col = signal, S+1 = GND) · 1 MΩ row g · Zener row h, band (cathode) toward the S column. Run the row-f GND chain in insulated wire, stripped only at the G columns —
a bare bus wire would short the signal pads it crosses. The eight plugs sit shoulder-to-shoulder: label the piezo cables S1–S8 before connecting.

LED feed: all three JST pins are wired (5V / DATA / GND) to match the strip harness, so the board feeds the strip's start — that share (≤ ~2 A worst case) flows through the pigtail, rail bridges, and rails: use ≥20 AWG there.
Keep the mid- and end-of-strip injection taps wired straight to the slab DC rail. Match JST pin order to your harness — buzz it out with a multimeter before first plug-in.

Ground the 74AHCT125's unused OE pins 4, 10, 13 and inputs 5, 9, 12. Golden rule: ESP32, shifter, strip, and all 8 piezos share one GND. Solder order: passives → IC → JST headers → female headers last (DevKit as jig; never solder it).

USB and PSU 5V may coexist (the DevKitC-1 has a protection diode), but unplug the LED-strip JST when flashing on USB-only power — USB can't feed the strip. Bench-test per the Phase 5 checklist before boxing.
